faq.q1: Which languages do you work with?
faq.a1: We cover a wide range of language pairs for translation and interpretation. Tell us your source and target languages and we'll confirm coverage and match you with the right native-speaking linguists.
faq.q2: How is AI actually used in my translation?
faq.a2: AI-assisted tools speed up first drafts, reuse translation memory, and flag terminology or consistency issues early. Every translation is still reviewed and finalized by a native-speaking human linguist before delivery — AI never has the final word.
faq.q3: How fast can you turn a project around?
faq.a3: It depends on length, language pair, and complexity. Share your content and deadline through the contact form and we'll confirm a realistic timeline before any work starts.
faq.q4: Can you match our existing terminology and style guide?
faq.a4: Yes. We build a glossary and style guide from your existing materials and preferences, then apply them consistently across every translator and project — see our terminology & style management service for details.
faq.q5: Do you offer interpretation for live events?
faq.a5: Yes, both on-site and remote (video or phone), in simultaneous or consecutive mode. Share your event date, format, and language pairs and we'll confirm interpreter availability.
faq.q6: How do I get a quote?
faq.a6: Use the contact form with your languages, content, and deadline, or email us directly at hello{'@'}amidas.si. We'll follow up with a scope and a quote.

svcTranslation.h1: Translation & localization that reads like it was written for your market.
svcTranslation.lead: We adapt documents, websites, software, and marketing content for each target market — not just translating words, but making sure tone, formatting, and cultural context land correctly.
svcTranslation.p1: Every project starts with understanding what the source content is trying to do — inform, persuade, instruct — and matching that intent in the target language, not just its words. A native-speaking linguist translates and reviews each document, so idioms, tone, and register carry over naturally instead of reading like a translation.
svcTranslation.p2: Localization goes further than translation: dates, currency, units, and formatting are adapted to local conventions, software and app strings are translated in context, and print-ready documents keep their original layout after translation.
svcTranslation.f1: Native-speaking translators for every language pair
svcTranslation.f2: Formatting and layout preserved across documents, websites, and apps
svcTranslation.f3: Cultural and regional adaptation, not just word-for-word translation
svcTranslation.f4: Consistent terminology across all translated content

svcInterpretation.h1: Interpretation for meetings, conferences, and live events.
svcInterpretation.lead: On-site and remote interpreters help you communicate confidently in real time, in the language pairs and format your event needs.
svcInterpretation.p1: Simultaneous interpretation keeps a live event moving in real time, ideal for conferences, webinars, and multi-language panels. Consecutive interpretation works better for smaller meetings, negotiations, and site visits, where the interpreter speaks after each part of the conversation.
svcInterpretation.p2: Interpreters can join on-site or remotely over video or phone, and we match each assignment to an interpreter experienced in your subject area — legal, technical, medical, or business — so nothing gets lost in translation when it matters most.
svcInterpretation.f3: Interpreters matched to your subject area

svcAiQa.h1: AI-assisted translation & QA, with a human always in the loop.
svcAiQa.lead: Translation memory and AI tools speed up first drafts and catch inconsistencies early — but every translation is reviewed and approved by a native-speaking linguist before it reaches you.
svcAiQa.p1: AI tools draft a first pass quickly by reusing your translation memory and applying your approved terminology, which shortens turnaround on large or recurring projects. Automated checks flag inconsistent terms, missed placeholders, and formatting issues before a linguist ever looks at the text.
svcAiQa.p2: That draft is only a starting point. A native-speaking linguist reviews and edits every segment for meaning, tone, and context — the parts AI still gets wrong — so the final translation reads naturally and holds up under scrutiny.
svcAiQa.f1: AI-assisted first drafts for faster turnaround
svcAiQa.f3: Every output reviewed and finalized by a human linguist

svcTerminology.h1: Terminology & style management that keeps every project consistent.
svcTerminology.lead: Shared glossaries and style guides make sure your brand voice and technical terms stay consistent — across languages, projects, and translators.
svcTerminology.p1: We build your glossary from the content you already have — past translations, product documentation, and any preferred terms you provide — then confirm it with you before it's applied to new work. A style guide captures tone, formatting conventions, and terms to avoid, so every translator works from the same playbook.
svcTerminology.p2: Both are living documents. As your product, market, or terminology evolves, we update the glossary and style guide and roll the changes into future projects, so consistency doesn't decay over time or across translators.

svcTerminology.f2: Style guide covering tone, formatting, and terminology

svcContent.p2: We work from a creative brief, existing brand guidelines, or source content you already have, and keep a consistent voice across every language and channel — website copy, ads, social posts, and product listings alike.

svcPartner.lead: One point of contact learns your business, terminology, and deadlines — so every project starts from context, not from scratch.
